rv.q: Director Lisa Portes' production simply hadn't fully come together by opening to light the essential fuses.

While this is a fine production of an early work by a celebrated playwright, I was hoping for further exploration of the role of art under oppressive systems, given the musical reference in the title and the fact that the play was inspired by a revolutionary writer.
Once the ball gets rolling, 'Two Sisters and a Piano' is an irresistible force.
Writers Theatre presents a thought-provoking production that's made even richer by its exquisite staging and fine performances.
San Miguel and Mendoza Castro draw the audience completely into their performances, and it is difficult to leave these compelling characters behind.
They are much more interesting than the play as a whole, which can't seem to decide exactly what it wants to be until the last fifteen minutes or so...
When they connect even in the face of all they've lost and the ongoing uncertainty facing their country as well as their own lives, it's poignant and heartbreaking.
The production is solid, although the Sunday performance I attended felt a bit under tempo. It's the play that comes up short.
Somewhat recommended, if only for the excellence of the overall production, “ Two Sisters and a Piano” runs at Writers Theatre through March 29 in Glencoe, IL.
I thought that every detail of this production was solid.
